prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: Link Inventory Audit — Q1 2025 (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Page title" · longest unbreakable unit 100px · widest one-line content 319px
  col 2: header "URL" · longest unbreakable unit 324px · widest one-line content 841px
  col 3: header "Last checked" · longest unbreakable unit 61px · widest one-line content 96px
  col 4: header "Status code" · longest unbreakable unit 47px · widest one-line content 86px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 720px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 720px wide (column widths sum to at most 719px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 720px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"Audit a set of page links and their most recent check results.","tasks":["Find a page by title or URL.","Associate each URL with its page, check date and status code.","Compare check dates and status codes across pages."],"relations":["Each row connects a page title and URL to the date and result of its link check.","The title and URL identify the same page; the date and status describe its check."],"roles":["The header row names four fields.","Each body row is one link record; the page title acts as a practical row identifier.","The date and status columns are compact lookup and comparison fields."],"keep_whole":["URL segments that cannot break naturally, including the longest 324px unit.","Words in page titles and headers.","Individual date and status-code units."],"may_wrap":["Page titles at spaces and natural punctuation.","URLs at available break opportunities, while keeping unbreakable segments intact.","Multiword headers and dates at natural break points when space requires it."],"same_scale":["The date and status columns serve similarly compact audit fields, though the date needs more room.","Body rows share the same four-column structure even when their heights differ."],"h_vs_v":"The URL needs a large minimum width to preserve its longest unbreakable segment; allocating more space to titles or compact audit fields reduces wrapping there but leaves URLs taller. Allowing vertical growth keeps the table within the viewport."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d3r2A, d3r0B.
Measured facts:
d3r2A: column widths [140, 355, 117, 107] px · table 720×627 px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 83, 106, 83, 106] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
d3r0B: column widths [150, 345, 117, 107] px · table 720×580 px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 83, 83, 83, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). Then either propose up to 3 improved designs (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or try an important unexplored idea) or, if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement, set "done": true. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
